items.claim: The Jeremiah-to-Hananiah reply in Jer.28.5-Jer.28.9 is a clean narrative unit bounded by a fresh third-person speaker-formula at its front seam and a shift back to Hananiah as actor at its back seam, with none of its own content misattributed to a divine formula.
items.evidence: Every WEB and Hebrew splice in the unit (oshb:Jer.28.5, oshb:Jer.28.6, oshb:Jer.28.9 and their web: pairs) collates byte-true against the staged text. The marked-verse inventory carries no petuchah, setumah, paseq, or ketiv/qere anywhere from oshb:Jer.28.4 through oshb:Jer.28.9, matching the disclosed silence exactly. Jeremiah's own words here carry no koh-amar formula of any kind, so the chapter's frame-ownership hazard (Hananiah speaking the divine formula elsewhere in this same chapter) does not touch this content.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah absence, span-scoped (WLC, single-witness; verified against the marks inventory)

items.claim: The bar-breaking counter-act and Hananiah's own koh-amar claim in Jer.28.10-Jer.28.11 are textually sound and correctly disclose the false prophet as the formula's speaker, but this unit's own account of its rejected alternative twice identifies neighboring material by narrative position rather than by verse.
items.evidence: The Hebrew at oshb:Jer.28.11 explicitly narrates Hananiah, not Yahweh, as the formula's speaker, matching the disclosure given; the consonantal spelling of Nebuchadnezzar there lacks the vav carried by the plene spelling used elsewhere in the surrounding chapters, confirming the defective-spelling claim; the petuchah and paseq claimed at oshb:Jer.28.11 both match the inventory, correctly disclosed as single-witness and count-only. Separately, this unit's own account of the rejected alternative twice identifies neighboring material by narrative position alone rather than by verse - once as "the row that opens this chapter" and once as "the row that follows" - where every comparable cross-reference elsewhere in this span is verse-anchored instead (the reply-formula parallel drawn to verse 5, for instance). A position-only description of this kind cannot be checked against the bytes on its own terms and stops describing the same material if the span is ever resequenced, unlike a verse number.
tier_citations: citation-anchoring discipline: verse-anchored vs. position-only cross-reference

items.claim: The commissioned reply in Jer.28.12-Jer.28.14 is correctly opened by a fresh word-event formula and correctly keeps the wood-to-iron reinterpretation together as one unit, and its claim of exactly two such formulas across the whole three-chapter complex is byte-accurate.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.28.12 opens with the vayehi-devar-YHWH formula; this and oshb:Jer.29.30 are the only two verses carrying that formula anywhere across Jer.27.1-Jer.29.32, and no verse in that same range carries either of the book's other two word-event shapes, confirmed against the book's own word-event count. The defective, vav-less spelling of Nebuchadnezzar recurs at oshb:Jer.28.14 exactly as it stood in the claim it answers at oshb:Jer.28.11. The petuchah disclosed at oshb:Jer.28.11 is correctly attributed to the preceding unit's own close rather than argued as this unit's own driver.
tier_citations: tier-1 vayehi-debar-YHWH word-event formula (byte, corpus count verified)

items.claim: The judgment scene in Jer.28.15-Jer.28.16 is soundly bounded, but its device-notes claim of a setumah at Jer.28.16 is not supported by the marked-verse inventory, and its WEB quotation of the same verse drops a closing quotation mark present in the staged source.
items.evidence: The byte-extracted parashah inventory carries no mark of any kind at oshb:Jer.28.16; the nearest actual mark is a petuchah at oshb:Jer.28.17, one verse past this unit's own end and a different type from the setumah claimed. Separately, the staged WEB source for Jer.28.16 closes Yahweh's embedded words with both a single quotation mark and the verse-final double quotation mark immediately after it; the quotation of the same verse (web:Jer.28.16) reproduces the single quotation mark that opens those embedded words but not the matching one that closes them, so the quotation does not fully match the staged source it claims to reproduce verbatim. Neither defect touches the boundary itself, which remains supported by the said-to-Hananiah reply-formula shared with this unit's own front seam and by the shift into third-person narration at the following verse, oshb:Jer.28.17.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah mark claim, unverified against the marks inventory (WLC)
WEB quotation fidelity, byte-level comparison against the staged source

items.claim: The one-verse fulfillment notice at Jer.28.17 is correctly isolated by its shift from quoted confrontation into third-person narrative report, and its parashah disclosure is accurate on both sides of the seam.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.28.16 carries no mark of any kind and oshb:Jer.28.17 carries a petuchah, exactly as disclosed. The verse itself is pure third-person narration with no quoted speech at all, contrasting with the direct address filling the verses immediately before it and with the wholly different epistolary opening that follows at oshb:Jer.29.1.
tier_citations: tier-1 mode shift, narration displacing quoted speech (byte-evident)

items.claim: The epistolary superscription in Jer.29.1-Jer.29.3 is correctly bounded as formula-free framing material ahead of the letter's actual content, with accurate parashah and name-spelling disclosure.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.28.17 carries a petuchah and oshb:Jer.29.3 carries a setumah, both correctly typed and disclosed at this unit's own front seam and end verse. Verses 1 through 3 contain no koh-amar, no imperative, and no direct second-person address, consistent with the claim that the superscription carries no oracular content of its own. Nebuchadnezzar's name is spelled plene, with the vav present, at both oshb:Jer.29.1 and oshb:Jer.29.3, matching the family of spelling that clusters at the letter's own opening before a different spelling family appears later in the same chapter, at oshb:Jer.29.21.
tier_citations: tier-1 epistolary superscription, absence of oracular formula (byte-evident)

items.claim: The letter's opening address in Jer.29.4-Jer.29.14 correctly keeps its three internal koh-amar recurrences inside one unit because none of them carries a frame-owner change or a fresh addressee, and its parashah and ketiv/qere disclosures are accurate.
items.evidence: The koh-amar formulas at oshb:Jer.29.4, oshb:Jer.29.8, and oshb:Jer.29.10 all remain addressed to the same exile audience named at verse 4, with no new named addressee introduced anywhere in this span; the next new addressee (the king and the city) is not named until oshb:Jer.29.16, outside this unit. The setumah at oshb:Jer.29.3, the petuchah at oshb:Jer.29.7, and the setumah at oshb:Jer.29.9 all match the marked-verse inventory exactly, correctly typed and disclosed at the front seam and interior. The ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.29.14 matches the inventory and is not one of the twelve doubled-note verses, consistent with the single-note disclosure given.
tier_citations: tier-1 koh-amar recurrence without frame-owner or addressee change (byte-evident)

items.claim: The judgment on the king and city in Jer.29.15-Jer.29.20 is honestly bounded with a disclosed, unresolved question over which side of the seam verse 15 belongs to, and its far edge and its disclosures are all accurate.
items.evidence: No formula marks whether the exiles' quoted claim at oshb:Jer.29.15 closes the promise beginning at oshb:Jer.29.4 or opens the judgment that follows, and the unit states this honestly rather than forcing a resolution either way. The fresh koh-amar at oshb:Jer.29.21, naming Ahab and Zedekiah directly for the first time, confirms the far-edge boundary chosen. The setumah marks claimed at oshb:Jer.29.15 and oshb:Jer.29.20 both match the marked-verse inventory, and the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.29.18 matches the inventory as a single, non-doubled note.
tier_citations: tier-1 koh-amar onset with fresh named addressees at the far seam (byte-evident)
